judge_assessment.explanation: The single hard failure is exact and I confirmed it in the source. worksheet.tex problem 2 prints a three-column table with six empty cells -- rows 'Printer A: $4t + 7$' and 'Printer B: $4t + 2$' against columns t = 1, 2, 3 -- then says 'Fill in the table, then solve $4t + 7 = 4t + 2$ and classify the equation.' verify.json id 2 is a single solve of '4*t+7-(4*t+2)' with expected [], and nothing else carries id 2. The six cells are exactly machine-checkable (11, 15, 19 and 6, 10, 14; the key states those very numbers in its solution paragraph), so they are not open responses that could excuse the omission -- they are checkable values the file simply does not record. The judge's added phrase 'and the printed classification' is fair here in a way it would not be elsewhere: the printed answer for problem 2 is the words 'no solution', and the bank prints '2. ---' for it rather than any bound text, so nothing ties the printed classification to the empty solution set. The rest of the sheet does not share this defect and the judge was right not to widen the claim -- ids 8, 9 and 10 each carry multiple entries, and the two genuinely open justifications (8c and 10b) are declared manual with reviewer-facing descs. Every value recomputes: w=4, no solution, 2x+6, x=7, no solution, infinitely many, m=3, 6x-3 with a=6, then no solution / infinitely many / x=8, then no solution.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 8 splits itself correctly across the trust boundary: id 8 carries an expand entry for 'Expand the left side' (3*(2*x-1) -> 6*x-3) AND a manual entry for part (c)'s justification, whose desc tells the reviewer what a correct argument contains ('matching x-coefficients with different constants forces no solution'). One problem, two response types, two correctly typed entries. This is the pattern seven other cases in this shard are missing.

Problem 9 declares three separate entries under one id -- a solve with expected [] for 8x-3=8x+1, an equiv for 4(x+2)=4x+8, and a solve with expected [8] for 5x-6=3x+10 -- one per printed \ansline. Per-slot verification done right, and the three parts are deliberately one of each classification.

Problems 8 and 10 print \noansline where the response is a paragraph, so the sheet does not offer a one-line blank for an argument. That small layout decision is what keeps the open items visibly different from the computational ones.

Problem 6 ($-2(4x - 6) + 5 = 17 - 8x$) is the strongest item: after distributing and combining, the left is $-8x + 17$ and the right is $17 - 8x$ -- the same expression with the terms swapped. A student who classifies by pattern-matching the printed strings gets it wrong; one who simplifies first gets it right. The key names exactly that: 'the two sides are the same expression written in a different order'.

root_causes.description: A table printed inside a problem is treated as decoration rather than as a set of response slots. Problem 2's six blank cells are printed for the student to fill and are the evidence that the two totals stay 5 apart, which is the whole argument for 'no solution' -- yet the coverage rule (one check per problem id, SKILL.md line 189) is satisfied by the single solve entry, so the gate chain passes with the table unrecorded.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 2 tabular: two data rows x three t-columns, all cells empty ('&  &  &  \\[0.35cm]')
verify.json contains exactly one entry with id 2: {"type": "solve", "expr": "4*t+7-(4*t+2)", "var": "t", "expected": []}
answer_key.pdf problem 2: 'at t = 1 they are 11 and 6, at t = 2 they are 15 and 10, at t = 3 they are 19 and 14' -- the six values exist in the key but in no check
SKILL.md line 189: 'verification hard-fails unless every problem id 1..N has at least one check'

root_causes.description: A verified empty solution set renders in the Quick Answers bank as '---', the identical glyph scripts/render_quick_answers.py reserves for manual-only ids. Problems 2, 5 and 10 are verified 'no solution' answers and all three print '---'. Worse, on a mixed id the empty list renders as an empty string inside a comma join: problem 9's bank line reads ', 4x + 8, 8' with a leading comma where the verified 'no solution' belongs.
evidence: verify.json ids 2, 5 and 10 are solve entries with expected []; id 9 holds three entries, the first with expected []
I called the module directly: render_entry([{'expected': []}]) returns '---', and render_entry with expecteds [[], '4*x+8', [8]] returns ', $4 x + 8$, 8'
scripts/render_quick_answers.py render_entry(): 'if not vals:  # manual-only: the worked solution is the answer' guards the same '---'

improvements.title: Problem 2's six printed table cells carry no verification entry
improvements.proposed_change: Give id 2 six eval entries -- '4*t+7' at t = 1, 2, 3 and '4*t+2' at t = 1, 2, 3 -- alongside the existing solve, exactly as ids 8, 9 and 10 of this same file already carry several entries. Enforce it generally: extend tests/check_layout.py to parse tabular environments inside a \problem segment, count empty data cells, and fail when the problem's verify entry count is lower than the number of blank cells the student is told to fill. Rendering the table's blank cells from the same data the checks read (the pattern SKILL.md already mandates for pgfplots charts) would make the two impossible to disagree.
improvements.regression_test: Add a fixture worksheet whose problem 1 prints a 2x3 table of empty cells with the instruction 'Fill in the table' against a verification JSON holding one entry for id 1, and assert check_layout.py exits non-zero naming the six uncovered cells. It exits 0 today.
improvements.expected_impact: Problem 2 is the sheet's model for why identical x-terms can never meet; the table is the evidence and is currently the only unverified thing on an otherwise well-covered sheet. This is the run's dominant systemic finding (61 cases).
improvements.risk: Medium. A cell-counting rule will fire on tables printed as given data (the reference tables in curr-202 and curr-232) rather than as response slots. Distinguish by whether the cells are empty in the source, and land warn-only for one run.

improvements.title: Verified 'no solution' answers print as '---' in the bank, and a mixed id prints a leading comma
improvements.proposed_change: In scripts/render_quick_answers.py, handle the empty-list expected explicitly before the generic list branch: an empty solution set is a verified answer, not a missing one, so _fmt([]) should return 'no solution' (or '\varnothing') rather than the empty string that render_entry then converts to '---'. That also fixes the join defect -- problem 9's line becomes 'no solution, $4x + 8$, 8' instead of ', 4x + 8, 8'. Manual-only ids keep printing '---' because render_entry's 'if not vals' branch is unchanged.
improvements.regression_test: Add a case rendering {"id": 1, "type": "solve", "expr": "x-x+1", "expected": []} beside {"id": 2, "type": "manual"} and assert the id-1 line reads 'no solution' while id 2 reads '---'; add a second case with expecteds [[], '4*x+8', [8]] under one id and assert the line has no leading comma. Today the first case prints '---' for both ids and the second prints ', $4 x + 8$, 8'.
improvements.expected_impact: Three of this sheet's ten bank entries stop being indistinguishable from unchecked items, and the malformed line at problem 9 is repaired. Affects every worksheet whose verification_targets include 'solve' on a no-solution or inconsistent equation -- which is the entire 'no-solution' facet of this topic.
improvements.risk: Low; bank-only text that check_answer_key.py does not parse. The one judgement call is the wording, and 'no solution' matches the three answer forms the worksheet directions name.

improvements.title: Problem 3's and problem 4's classification prose have no manual companion
improvements.proposed_change: Problems 1 through 7 all end with 'and classify the equation', and the classification is recoverable from the solve/equiv result, so no change is needed there. Problem 3 additionally asks the student to say what the identity means for Sam's and Dana's two perimeter expressions, which is the same open-reasoning shape the sheet already declares manual at 8(c) and 10(b). Add a manual entry under id 3 with a desc ('both expressions describe the same perimeter, so the equation is true for every x'), keeping this sheet's own convention consistent across all four items that ask for meaning rather than a value.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture problem whose stem contains 'classify' plus an interpretive clause and only a solve entry; assert the explanation lint from the systemic fix names it. No such lint exists today.
improvements.expected_impact: Small; this sheet already handles the two hardest open items correctly, so this is consistency rather than a new capability.
improvements.risk: Low, and there is a real argument the current treatment is fine, since the interpretive clause in problem 3 is one phrase inside a stem whose printed answer is the classification. Treat as polish, not a blocker.

case_summary: This is the best-verified sheet of my ten and it was rejected for a single, real omission. Ids 8, 9 and 10 each declare several entries -- one per printed \ansline -- and the two genuinely open justifications (8c, 10b) are typed manual with reviewer criteria and printed with \noansline so no one-line blank invites a paragraph. Every classification recomputes, and problem 6 is a well-built trap where the two sides are the same expression with terms swapped. The rejection rests on problem 2: six blank table cells the student is told to fill (11, 15, 19 and 6, 10, 14, values the answer key states) against one solve entry recording only the empty solution set. Two things the judge did not raise, both in the Quick Answers bank: verified 'no solution' answers at ids 2, 5 and 10 print '---', the glyph reserved for manual-only items, and id 9's mixed line renders as ', 4x + 8, 8' with a leading comma where the verified empty solution set should be.
